    What is real

    Planet, Moon and Galilean-moon positions and spin axes are computed for the current date with astronomy-engine (MIT). Planet sizes, masses, temperatures and atmospheres are published values. Surface maps: Solar System Scope (CC BY 4.0) from NASA mission data; Earth from NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble. The 10,130 stars are from the HYG database v4.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0, astronexus.com) with Hipparcos and Gaia distances. Nebulae, clusters and galaxies sit at their catalogued sky positions (d3-celestial) and published distances. Exoplanets use NASA Exoplanet Archive values.

    Approximate: the phases of moons other than ours and Jupiter's four, terrain detail finer than the source maps, the look of exoplanets, and the overall shape of the Milky Way. Stars beyond the catalogue (more than ~400 ly from the Sun, fainter than the eye can see) are generated to fill space and are marked as such.
